# Runtime verification

`tools/verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js` is a **sandboxed runtime verifier** that runs each adapter in a Node `vm` context with mocked browser APIs and inspects the returned envelope. It catches bugs `bb-eval` cannot.
10→
## Why both checkers?

| Tool | What it sees | What it misses |
|---|---|---|
| `bb-eval` (static) | `@meta` block, source keywords, URL constants, no-creds, and whether the body compiles as the runtime's single expression | Undefined variables at call time, envelope shape of actual returns |
| `verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js` (sandbox) | Envelope shape, error paths, basic meta validation | Real DOM selectors, real API responses, real timing |

You need both. The static check is fast and catches contract violations; the runtime verifier catches **bugs the static check was never going to find**.

20→## Why this tool exists (2026-06-19 incident — corrected 2026-09-07)

SM-2.8 attempted to **really test** all 16 social-media adapters via bb-browser MCP, but `browser_eval` started returning `{}` mid-session and `browser_close_all` only closed tracked tabs. The MCP eval channel was broken.

The fix was a sandbox runtime-shape verifier — run the adapter in Node `vm` with mocked `bb.goto` / `bb.eval` / `window`, inspect the returned object.

The verifier's first cross-domain run (SM-2.8) flagged 14 ecommerce/pharma-data adapters (`1688/*` × 12 + `yaozh-auth` + `yaopinzhongbiao`) as "broken anonymous-function syntax". **That conclusion was inverted.** A 2026-09-07 runtime audit corrected the record:

- The real runtime (`bb-browser site.ts`) strips the first `@meta` block and evals the remaining body as **one expression**, `(body)(args)`. The bare single-function format (`async function(args) { ... }`) is exactly what the runtime expects — those 14 files were **never broken**.
- What actually broke 43 adapters (ybm 9, 1688 11, xhs 16, yaozh 7) was the **June-29 rewrite** into multi-statement format (top-level `const` + `module.exports`): wrapped as an expression, `(const ...; module.exports = ...)(args)` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'const'` at runtime.
30→- `node --check` and standalone-module parsing report the **opposite** verdict, because they parse the file as a module rather than as an expression. bb-eval's Check 0 was replaced on 2026-09-07 to compile `(body)` — runtime-identical (see [bb-eval](bb-eval.md)).
- The sandbox verifier itself calls adapters through a named-export (module) convention, which is why it passed the June-29 rewrites that the runtime rejects. **Re-aligning the verifier to `(body)(args)` semantics is part of SM-2.9.**

Lesson: every execution environment (runtime eval, Node module, vm sandbox) has its own parse semantics — a "syntax error" verdict is only meaningful relative to the environment that will actually run the code.

## How to use it

```bash
node tools/verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js \
  --adapter ~/.bb-browser/sites/xiaohongshu/adapters/auth.js
40→
# Multiple adapters
node tools/verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js \
  --adapters ~/.bb-browser/sites/xiaohongshu/adapters/

# With a custom mock for INITIAL_STATE
node tools/verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js \
  --adapter ./auth.js \
  --mock '{"INITIAL_STATE":{"user":{"userInfo":{"_value":{"userId":"abc"}}}}}'
```
50→
Exit code is **0** if all adapters PASS, **1** otherwise. Output is JSON when `--json` is passed.

## What the sandbox provides

| API | Mock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `bb.goto(url)` | records the call, resolves to `{ url }` | Lets adapters navigate |
| `bb.eval(js)` | executes in vm context, returns last expression | Lets adapters read page state |
| `bb.fetch(url, opts)` | records the call, returns mock JSON | Lets adapters call APIs |

137→# ----- Check 0.5: no ghost API calls -----
# The runtime injects no `bb` global (site.ts / site-runner.ts both evaluate
# `(body)(args)` in the raw page context). bb.goto/bb.eval/bb.fetch and the
140→# page-handle chain they returned were a phantom API — any real call throws
# ReferenceError in production (soul.md 2026-09-07). Comment mentions are fine.
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  GHOST_HITS="$(node -e '
    const fs = require("fs");
    const NL = String.fromCharCode(10);
    const lines = fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").split(NL);
    const re = /(^|[^.\w])(?:await\s+)?(?:bb|page|probe|here)\.(goto|eval|evaluate|wait|\$eval|\$\$eval)\s*\(/;
    const hits = [];
    lines.forEach((ln, i) => {
150→      if (/^\s*(\*|\/\/)/.test(ln)) return;
      const t = ln.replace(/\/\/.*$/, "");
      if (re.test(t)) hits.push((i + 1) + ": " + ln.trim().slice(0, 60));
    });
    process.stdout.write(hits.slice(0, 3).join(NL));
  ' "$ADAPTER")"
  if [[ -n "$GHOST_HITS" ]]; then
    record FAIL "no-ghost-api" "Adapter calls the phantom bb.*/page.* API (no bb global exists at runtime): $GHOST_HITS"
  else
    record PASS "no-ghost-api" "No phantom bb.*/page.* calls."
160→  fi
  unset GHOST_HITS
fi

if [[ -z "$DOMAIN" ]]; then
  # Domain detection. @meta.domain is used inconsistently across the codebase:
  #   - pharma-data / social-media adapters set it to the contract name ("pharma-data", "social-media")
  #   - ecommerce adapters set it to a hostname ("s.1688.com")
  # So: first honor explicit contract-name values, then fall back to hostname heuristics
  # on both @meta.domain and @meta.name.
170→  case "$META_DOMAIN" in
    ecommerce|pharma-data|social-media) DOMAIN="$META_DOMAIN" ;;
  esac

  if [[ -z "$DOMAIN" ]]; then
    # Hostname heuristics — check both domain and name fields.
    HAYSTACK="${META_DOMAIN} ${NAME}"
    case "$HAYSTACK" in
      *yaozh.com*|*data.yaozh.com*|*yaozh/*) DOMAIN=pharma-data ;;
      *xiaohongshu*|*xhs*|*xhslink*|*twitter.com*|*x.com*|*twitter/*|*bilibili*|*b23.tv*|*bilibili/*|*discord.com*|*discord.gg*|*discord/*|*telegram*|*t.me*) DOMAIN=social-media ;;
180→      *ysbang*|*1688*|*ybm100.com*|*jd.com*|*pdd.com*|*taobao.com*|*111.com.cn*|*1yaocheng*|*tmall*|*yaoex*|*fangkuaiyi*) DOMAIN=ecommerce ;;
      *) DOMAIN=unknown ;;
    esac
  fi
fi

# ----- Code window: first 50 lines AFTER the @meta block -----
# The URL-constant rule counts CODE lines, not front matter: June-29 files carry
# @disclaimer headers + expanded @meta that alone exceed 50 physical lines.
meta_end_line="$(awk '/\/\* *@meta/{f=1} f && /\*\//{print NR; exit}' "$ADAPTER")"
190→if [[ -n "$meta_end_line" ]]; then
  CODE_WINDOW="$(sed -n "$((meta_end_line + 1)),$((meta_end_line + 50))p" "$ADAPTER")"
else
  CODE_WINDOW="$(head -n 50 "$ADAPTER")"
fi

# ----- PHR-1: domain must be pharma-data if --domain pharma-data -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" ]]; then
  META_DOMAIN_VAL="$(meta_get '.domain')"
  if [[ "$META_DOMAIN_VAL" == "pharma-data" ]]; then
200→    record PASS "PHR-1 domain-set" "@meta.domain is 'pharma-data'."
  else
    record FAIL "PHR-1 domain-set" "@meta.domain must be 'pharma-data', got: ${META_DOMAIN_VAL:-empty}"
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-2: dbkey declared -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" ]]; then
  DBKEY="$(meta_get '.dbKey')"
  if [[ -n "$DBKEY" && "$DBKEY" != "null" ]]; then
210→    record PASS "PHR-2 dbkey-declared" "@meta.dbKey is '${DBKEY}'."
  else
    record FAIL "PHR-2 dbkey-declared" "@meta.dbKey is missing."
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-4: list and item exported (skip for helpers) -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" ]]; then
  KIND="$(meta_get '.kind')"
  if [[ "$KIND" == "helper" ]]; then
220→    record PASS "PHR-4 helper-structure" "Helper adapter (kind: helper) does not require list/item."
  else
    if grep -q "async function list\b" "$ADAPTER"; then
      record PASS "PHR-4 list-function" "Adapter exports a 'list' function."
    else
      record FAIL "PHR-4 list-function" "Adapter must export an 'async function list'."
    fi
    if grep -q "async function item\b" "$ADAPTER"; then
      record PASS "PHR-4 item-function" "Adapter exports an 'item' function."
    else
230→      record FAIL "PHR-4 item-function" "Adapter must export an 'async function item'."
    fi
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-5: record shape (skip for helpers) -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" && "$KIND" != "helper" ]]; then
  if { grep -Eq "\bdbKey[:,]" "$ADAPTER" || grep -q "dbKey\b" "$ADAPTER"; } \
      && { grep -Eq "\bid[:,]" "$ADAPTER" || grep -q "\bid\b" "$ADAPTER"; } \
      && { grep -Eq "\burl:" "$ADAPTER" || grep -q "\burl[,}]" "$ADAPTER"; } \
240→      && { grep -Eq "\bfields[:,]" "$ADAPTER" || grep -q "fields\b" "$ADAPTER"; }; then
    record PASS "PHR-5 record-shape" "Adapter return contains dbKey, id, url, fields keys."
  else
    record FAIL "PHR-5 record-shape" "Adapter must return Record objects with dbKey, id, url, fields."
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-6: ID discriminator (skip for helpers) -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" && "$KIND" != "helper" ]]; then
  if grep -qE "(isNumeric|isBase64|/\\^\?\\\\d\\+\\\$/|\\.test\\(.*\\d|Number\\(.*id|base64.*test|test.*base64)" "$ADAPTER"; then
250→    record PASS "PHR-6 id-detect" "item() function contains ID-type discrimination logic."
  else
    record WARN "PHR-6 id-detect" "item() should detect numeric vs base64 ID format. Static check cannot verify runtime behavior."
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-7: authStatus field (skip for helpers) -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" && "$KIND" != "helper" ]]; then
  if grep -q "authStatus" "$ADAPTER"; then
    record PASS "PHR-7 auth-status" "Adapter returns authStatus field."
260→  else
    record FAIL "PHR-7 auth-status" "Every Record/Detail must include authStatus: 'public'|'soft_vip'|'hard_wall'."
  fi
fi

# ----- PHR-8: canonical adapter names -----
if [[ "$DOMAIN" == "pharma-data" ]]; then
  case "$ADAPTER_LOCAL" in
    auth|list|item|search|export|related|yaozh-auth)
      record PASS "PHR-8 canonical-name" "'${ADAPTER_LOCAL}' is a canonical pharma-data adapter name." ;;
270→    *-list|*-detail|*-list.js|*-detail.js)
      record FAIL "PHR-8 canonical-name" "Adapter names like '${ADAPTER_LOCAL}' are forbidden. One adapter per dbKey, exporting list()+item()." ;;
    *)
      record WARN "PHR-8 canonical-name" "'${ADAPTER_LOCAL}' is not in the canonical P0/P1 set for pharma-data." ;;

if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    const fs = require("fs");
    const NL = String.fromCharCode(10);
    const lines = fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").split(NL);
    const re = /(^|[^.\w])(?:await\s+)?(?:bb|page|probe|here)\.(goto|eval|evaluate|wait|\$eval|\$\$eval)\s*\(/;
    const hits = [];
    lines.forEach((ln, i) => {
      if (/^\s*(\*|\/\/)/.test(ln)) return;
      const t = ln.replace(/\/\/.*$/, "");

    });
    process.stdout.write(hits.slice(0, 3).join(NL));

type: wiki-concept
last_updated: 2026-06-28

# Auth tiers

Authentication is the **hardest** part of writing an adapter. Every domain contract declares an auth model and every adapter must declare what tier it needs.
10→
There are **two different taxonomies** in the repo, used in different domains:

| Domain | Taxonomy | Per-adapter field |
|---|---|---|
| Ecommerce (and the universal `playbook`) | tier-1 / tier-2 / tier-3 (effort-based) | implicit |
| Pharma-data | `public` / `soft_vip` / `hard_wall` (data access) | `authStatus` |
| Social-media | `anonymous` / `auth_read` / `auth_write` (functional) | `accessTier` (declared) + `authStatus` (returned) |

The ecommerce tier model is **how to implement** the adapter. The pharma-data and social-media tier models are **what the site returns**. An adapter implements tier-2 to declare `accessTier: auth_read`.
20→
## Ecommerce tier system (implementation effort)

The playbook at `docs/claude/methodology/reverse-engineering/playbook.md` defines this 3-tier system. It answers "how much work is this adapter?".

| Tier | Auth | How to find it | Effort | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cookie only, naive `fetch` | Capture; request works with just `credentials: 'include'`. | ~1 min | Public product page, no personalization |
| 2 | Bearer + CSRF, or signed body | Look in captured headers; find token in `localStorage` / cookies. | ~3 min | ysbang most APIs, jd cart, pdd order list |
| 3 | Webpack injection / Pinia store / page-runtime signing | Token is built per-request inside JS; you must call into the page's own modules. | ~10–30 min | XHS signing (`x-s`/`x-t`), yaoex AES price decryption |
30→
**AGENTS.md #3:** "Tier-2/Tier-3 is the default assumption. Cookie-only is the exception, only for genuinely public pages." If your `search` adapter is tier-1 on a logged-in B2C site, you are almost certainly wrong — re-check by capturing network with `bb-browser network --with-body` while logged in.

## Pharma-data access levels (data access)

`docs/claude/contracts/pharma-data/v1.md` defines three access levels for **records**:

| Level | Meaning | Adapter behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `public` | Anyone can read. No login. | Adapter reads and returns full data. |
40→| `soft_vip` | Record shows up in the list, but detail fields are gated (literally shows "查看" / "view" button). | Adapter returns `vipGatedFields: [...field names...]`, **clears** the field values, and tells the agent how to upgrade. Never invents values. |
| `hard_wall` | The whole database is behind login; nothing renders for anonymous users. | Adapter returns `authStatus: hard_wall` with an explicit hint pointing to the `yaozh-auth` helper. No data is fabricated. |

The `authStatus` field is **the level that was actually in effect for this call**, not the site's theoretical maximum.

## Social-media access tiers (functional)

`docs/claude/contracts/social-media/v1.md` defines three tiers based on **what the agent is trying to do**:

| Tier | Meaning | Adapters that declare it |
50→|---|---|---|
| `anonymous` | Works logged-out. | `auth`, `search` (partial), `feed` (partial on some sites) |
| `auth_read` | Login required, but only to read. | `search`, `feed`, `post-detail`, `comments`, `user`, `user-notes`, `notifications`, `unread` |
| `auth_write` | Login required AND the account must be in good standing (not captcha-throttled, not rate-limited). | `like`, `favorite`, `comment-post`, `follow`, `post-create`, plus P1 writes |

`@meta.accessTier` declares the **minimum** tier the adapter needs. The returned `authStatus` reflects the tier **in effect for this call**.

## How these interact

| If the site is tier-3 to implement AND the data is auth_read | The adapter must do tier-3 (webpack injection / runtime signing) just to expose auth_read functionality. |
60→| If the data is hard_wall | The adapter returns `authStatus: hard_wall` regardless of how the implementation works. |

title: Response envelope
type: wiki-concept
last_updated: 2026-06-28

# Response envelope

Every adapter returns the **same top-level envelope**, regardless of domain. The envelope is what makes adapter outputs chainable.
10→
## Universal shape

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,                              // false ⇒ error/hint/action MUST be set
  "authStatus": "anonymous|auth_read|auth_write|public|soft_vip|hard_wall",
  "data": <domain-specific payload | null>,
  "constraints": { /* list adapters only */ },
  "pagination": { /* list adapters only */ },
20→  "recommendedNextActions": [ /* always except `auth` */ ],
  "error": "LOGIN_REQUIRED",               // present only when ok=false
  "hint":  "human-readable explanation",
  "action": "stop_and_wait_for_human"
}
```

The **domain-specific payload** (`data`) follows the contract for the domain. See:

- Ecommerce: [reference/ecommerce-product.md](../reference/ecommerce-product.md), [reference/ecommerce-order.md](../reference/ecommerce-order.md), [reference/ecommerce-cart.md](../reference/ecommerce-cart.md).
30→- Pharma-data: [reference/pharma-data-record.md](../reference/pharma-data-record.md).
- Social-media: [reference/social-media-note.md](../reference/social-media-note.md).

## Why an envelope?

Three reasons:

1. **Agent chaining.** The agent doesn't have to learn the shape of each adapter's return; it learns the envelope once and follows `recommendedNextActions`.
2. **Uniform error handling.** `error` + `hint` + `action` is the same triple across domains. The agent's "what to do next" code is one switch statement on `action`.
3. **Honest constraints.** `requestedConstraints` / `executedConstraints` / `deferredConstraints` tell the agent what was **actually** applied, not what was assumed. This prevents the agent from trusting the result for a constraint that was silently dropped.
40→
## Error code enum (each code bound to one action)

The `error` field is **a fixed enum** per domain. `action` is **bound to the error** — adapters MUST NOT invent new action values for these codes.

### Universal errors

| `error` | When | `action` |
|---|---|---|
| `LOGIN_REQUIRED` | Site requires login. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |
50→| `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED` | Site popped a captcha. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Frequency cap hit. | `backoff_and_retry` |
| `IP_BLOCKED` | IP banned / region-restricted. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Object doesn't exist or was deleted. | `abort` |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | No access (private / blocked). | `abort` |
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Cookie / token expired. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |

### Ecommerce-specific

| `error` | When | `action` |
60→|---|---|---|

# Response envelope

Every adapter returns the **same top-level envelope**, regardless of domain. The envelope is what makes adapter outputs chainable.
10→
## Universal shape

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,                              // false ⇒ error/hint/action MUST be set
  "authStatus": "anonymous|auth_read|auth_write|public|soft_vip|hard_wall",
  "data": <domain-specific payload | null>,
  "constraints": { /* list adapters only */ },
  "pagination": { /* list adapters only */ },
20→  "recommendedNextActions": [ /* always except `auth` */ ],
  "error": "LOGIN_REQUIRED",               // present only when ok=false
  "hint":  "human-readable explanation",
  "action": "stop_and_wait_for_human"
}
```

The **domain-specific payload** (`data`) follows the contract for the domain. See:

- Ecommerce: [reference/ecommerce-product.md](../reference/ecommerce-product.md), [reference/ecommerce-order.md](../reference/ecommerce-order.md), [reference/ecommerce-cart.md](../reference/ecommerce-cart.md).
30→- Pharma-data: [reference/pharma-data-record.md](../reference/pharma-data-record.md).
- Social-media: [reference/social-media-note.md](../reference/social-media-note.md).

## Why an envelope?

Three reasons:

1. **Agent chaining.** The agent doesn't have to learn the shape of each adapter's return; it learns the envelope once and follows `recommendedNextActions`.
2. **Uniform error handling.** `error` + `hint` + `action` is the same triple across domains. The agent's "what to do next" code is one switch statement on `action`.
3. **Honest constraints.** `requestedConstraints` / `executedConstraints` / `deferredConstraints` tell the agent what was **actually** applied, not what was assumed. This prevents the agent from trusting the result for a constraint that was silently dropped.
40→
## Error code enum (each code bound to one action)

The `error` field is **a fixed enum** per domain. `action` is **bound to the error** — adapters MUST NOT invent new action values for these codes.

| `error` | When | `action` |
|---|---|---|
| `LOGIN_REQUIRED` | Site requires login. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |

| `RATE_LIMITED` | Frequency cap hit. | `backoff_and_retry` |
| `IP_BLOCKED` | IP banned / region-restricted. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Object doesn't exist or was deleted. | `abort` |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | No access (private / blocked). | `abort` |
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Cookie / token expired. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` |

| `error` | When | `action` |

## Reverse-engineering tier expectations

Every ecommerce adapter except `auth` is expected to be **tier 2 or tier 3**:

| Tier | Auth | Effort | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cookie only, naive `fetch` | ~1 min | Public product pages without personalization |
| 2 | Bearer + CSRF / signed body | ~3 min | jd cart, pdd order list, ysbang most APIs |
210→| 3 | Webpack module injection / Pinia store / page-bound runtime | ~10-30 min | Pinned tokens, signed payloads only built inside the SPA |

If your `search` adapter is tier 1 on a logged-in B2C site, you are almost certainly wrong. Re-check by capturing network with `bb-browser network --with-body` while logged in.

## Versioning

This is `v1`. Future versions land at `docs/claude/contracts/ecommerce/v2.md` with a migration note pointing back. v1 stays frozen so existing adapters keep their evaluation reproducible.

## Open questions for v2

220→- Do we need a `category` adapter (browse by category tree)? Currently considered out-of-scope; agents should use `search` with a category filter argument.
- Should `checkout-preview` accept an explicit `couponIds[]` argument, or always return all applicable coupons and let the caller filter? Leaning toward the former.
- For multi-store B2B, should `search` be implicitly scoped to current store, or take a `storeId` arg? Current call: implicit, with `executedConstraints` declaring the active store.

Every adapter — read or write, list or single — returns this envelope. `recommendedNextActions` lets the agent chain calls without learning each site's idiosyncrasies.

200→```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,                                  // false ⇒ error/hint/action MUST be set
  "data": <Note | Note[] | User | Comment[] | WriteReceipt | null>,
  "authStatus": "anonymous" | "auth_read" | "auth_write",
  "constraints": { /* list adapters only; see §6.2 */ },
  "pagination": { /* list adapters only; see §6.3 */ },
  "recommendedNextActions": [ /* always except `auth` */ ],
  "error": "LOGIN_REQUIRED",                   // present only when ok=false
  "hint": "Run `auth` adapter, then hand control to human for login.",
210→  "action": "stop_and_wait_for_human"
}
```

### 6.1 Error codes (fixed enum, each bound to one action)

The `error` field MUST be one of:

| `error` | When | `action` | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
220→| `LOGIN_REQUIRED` | Site requires login to read. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` | Call `auth`; wait for human login. |
| `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED` | Site popped a captcha. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` | Human solves in-page, then retry. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Frequency cap hit (common on XHS writes). | `backoff_and_retry` | Wait 60–300s, then retry. Do NOT retry immediately. |
| `SIGNATURE_FAILED` | Request signature rejected (XHS `x-s`/`x-t` stale). | `refresh_and_retry` | Re-capture signature, re-issue. |
| `IP_BLOCKED` | IP banned / region-restricted. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` | Change proxy / environment; wait. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | noteId / userId doesn't exist or was deleted. | `abort` | Object unreachable; skip. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | No access (private note / blocked). | `abort` | Skip. |
| `CONTENT_REJECTED` | Write content rejected (banned words, etc.). | `abort` | Revise content; retry. |
| `WRITE_FAILED` | Generic write failure. | `retry_or_abort` | One retry; abort if still failing. |
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Cookie / token expired. | `stop_and_wait_for_human` | Re-login. |
230→| `NAVIGATE_REQUIRED` | The adapter reads a page/SPA state that the current tab doesn't hold. There is no `bb.goto` at runtime (the runtime evaluates the adapter once in the raw page context), so the adapter asks the agent to open the URL and re-run. | `open <url>` | Open the URL given in `action`, wait for the page/SPA to settle, then re-run the same adapter with the same args. |

`action` is bound to the error — adapters MUST NOT invent new action values for these codes (`NAVIGATE_REQUIRED`'s action is the one dynamic form: `open <url>`).

### 6.2 Constraints (list adapters)

List adapters (`search`, `feed`, `user-notes`, `comments`, `notifications`) MUST populate the constraint trio. Be honest: do not mark a constraint `executed` if you only acknowledged it.

```jsonc
"constraints": {
240→  "requestedConstraints": { "keyword": "咖啡", "sort": "latest", "type": "video" },
  "executedConstraints":   { "keyword": "咖啡", "sort": "latest" },
  "deferredConstraints":   { "type": "video" }   // not applied; tell the agent why in a hint
}
```

### 6.3 Pagination (list adapters)

Hybrid shape — surface both cursor and page so the agent picks the most robust path. `nextArgs` lets the agent copy-paste to the next call without understanding cursor semantics.

250→```jsonc
"pagination": {
  "page": 2,                                   // current page, 1-based
  "pageSize": 20,                              // count actually returned this page
  "hasMore": true,                             // raw site has_more flag
  "cursor": "next_cursor_string",              // cursor for cursor-based sites
  "nextArgs": { "cursor": "next_cursor_string" } // agent can pass this object directly as the next call's args
}
```

Chains adapters. Example after `search`:

```jsonc
"recommendedNextActions": [
  { "adapter": "post-detail", "args": { "noteId": "abc", "xsecToken": "..." }, "why": "View full content of the top result." },
  { "adapter": "comments",    "args": { "noteId": "abc" },                       "why": "See engagement on the top result." }
]

content.text:
Excellent first-hand data. Let me also quickly check:Got it—thanks for the quick audit. The ecommerce TEMPLATE missing error-envelope is a clear gap (no check at all, and the contract doesn't list it), while PHR-8's dbKey quirk is a known contract-vs-eval mismatch that needs fixing. Templates failing on no-ghost-api and ysbang 1688 search-by-price hitting forbidden-name are straightforward blockers. bb-eval not executable and the envelope inconsistency (success vs ok vs actual 1688 success) are bigger product issues for consumers.

SKILL gaps around bb.goto in the playbook, wiki author-loop still referencing bb-browser, and ma-browser v0.13 freeze output format all need alignment. CLI examples still say bb-browser site but the CLI is now ma-browser—that's a doc issue.

For the PRD, framing it as "bb-adapter-evolver (aligned with ma-browser v0.13)" and breaking it into M0–M4 milestones with Q*/ E*/ C*/ S*/ H*/ D* IDs makes sense. The envelope unification (or honest dual-schema) in M2 is important, and mentioning the local uncommitted edits in ~/.bb-browser/sites/ is honest.

1→# Ecommerce Adapter Templates

This directory contains contract-compliant reference adapters and a standard template.

## Structure

```
ecommerce/
├── TEMPLATE.js          ← Standard template with all required contract fields
10→├── reference/
│   └── search.js        ← ysbang/search (13/13 bb-eval pass, the gold standard)
└── fixed/
    ├── auth.js           ← Fixed: added HOME_URL constant (was 1 fail)
    ├── cart-update.js    ← Fixed: added HOME_URL + readOnly check (was 2 fail)
    ├── cart-remove.js    ← Already compliant (was false positive from bb-eval bug)
    ├── add-to-cart.js    ← Already compliant (was false positive)
    ├── checkout.js       ← Already compliant (was false positive)
    ├── select-best-add.js ← Already compliant (was false positive)
    ├── store-select.js   ← Already compliant (was false positive)
20→    ├── switch-store.js   ← Already compliant (was false positive)
    └── product-detail.js ← Fixed: added HOME_URL constant (was 1 fail)
```

## How to use

1. Copy `TEMPLATE.js` as your starting point
2. Replace `EXAMPLE_SITE` with your actual site name
3. Run `tools/bb-eval <your-adapter.js>` — must get 0 fail
4. Warnings are OK (they indicate areas for improvement)
30→
## bb-eval bug fix (2026-05-18)

The `meta_get()` function used `jq -r '.field // empty'` which treats `false` and `0` 
as missing (jq's `//` operator is "alternative", not "default"). This caused adapters 
with `"readOnly": false` to falsely fail the meta-field-readOnly check.

**Fix**: Added `meta_has()` function using `jq -e --arg k "$key" 'has($k) and (.[$k] != null)'`
which correctly checks field existence regardless of value.

40→Affected adapters: cart-remove, add-to-cart, checkout, select-best-add, store-select,

type: wiki-reference
last_updated: 2026-06-28

# Anti-patterns

The catalog of mistakes observed in past adapter work. Each entry: what was done, why it was wrong, and how to avoid it. **Read this before authoring.**
10→
## Filter explosion

**Done:** Created `search-by-price`, `search-by-factory`, `search-by-provider`, `search-by-expiration`, `search-by-free-shipping`, `search-with-filters`, `search-filters`, `search-plan`, ... as separate adapters.

**Why wrong:** Each duplicates ~200 lines of search-page navigation. Agents don't know which to call. Reviewers can't tell if `search-by-price` and `search-by-factory` use the same page.

**Avoid:** Filters are `search` arguments, not adapters. One `search` adapter with `keyword`, `page`, `pageSize`, `sort`, and any other filter args. `bb-eval` rejects `search-by-*` patterns.

## Stubbed sessions
20→
**Done:** Hard-coded test cookies in the adapter with `// TODO: replace before commit` comments. Always shipped with the stub.

**Why wrong:** The adapter appears to work in CI but fails for every real user. The TODO comment becomes a permanent fixture.

**Avoid:** Per AGENTS.md #5, **stop and ask the human**. Don't paper over login. The human logs in via the browser; the adapter reads the cookie at call time.

## Lying about constraints

**Done:** Marked `factory` as `executedConstraints` when the code only put it in the `deferredConstraints` list. The agent downstream trusted the result and skipped a follow-up call.
30→
**Why wrong:** The constraint trio is a lie-detector. Once the lie is in, every agent that consumes the adapter makes wrong assumptions about what was filtered.

**Avoid:** Before committing, ask: "if I gave this envelope to an agent that knew nothing about my site, would it correctly predict what was filtered?" If not, fix the trio. If `deferredConstraints` is non-empty, `recommendedNextActions` MUST contain a corresponding entry. `bb-eval constraint-tracking` checks this.

## Missing destination URL

**Done:** Adapter starts with `async function(args) { const token = ...` and never references the URL it's bound to.

**Why wrong:** Reader (human or agent) cannot tell what page this is for. Anti-debugging, anti-review.
40→

title: Choosing a domain
type: wiki-domain
last_updated: 2026-06-28
---

# Choosing a domain

When you sit down to author an adapter for a new site, the **first** decision is which contract to use. Get this wrong and the rest of the work is fighting the contract instead of authoring the adapter.
10→
## The three-question test

Answer these three questions about the **user's primary intent** for the adapter:

| Question | If yes | If no |
|---|---|---|
| **Q1. Does the site have a cart → checkout → order flow?** | Ecommerce candidate. | Skip ecommerce. |
| **Q2. Are records (data documents) the primary content?** | Pharma-data candidate. | Skip pharma-data. |
| **Q3. Is user-generated content + social graph the primary content?** | Social-media candidate. | None of these — escalate. |
20→
## Decision matrix

| Q1 cart/checkout | Q2 records | Q3 UGC+social | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | — | `ecommerce` |
| No | Yes | — | `pharma-data` |
| No | No | Yes | `social-media` |
| No | No | No | **None — escalate.** |
| Yes | Yes | — | **Both — pick by primary use case.** |
30→| Yes | — | Yes | **Both — pick by primary use case.** |

When multiple domains match, **pick by the user's primary use case for this adapter**, not by what the site as a whole does. A platform with both a shop and a social feed can have both ecommerce and social-media adapters; each follows its own contract.

## Worked examples

| Site | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jd.com` | ✅ | — | — | ecommerce | B2C marketplace, classic cart+order |
| `mall.yaoex.com` | ✅ | — | — | ecommerce | B2B wholesale, cart+order (Phase 3) |
40→| `db.yaozh.com` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | pharma-data | Data lookup; no cart/order; no UGC |
| `xiaohongshu.com` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | social-media | UGC with social graph; no cart |
| `taobao.com` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ecommerce | Has cart and order (note: shop recommendations are not UGC) |
| `weibo.com` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | social-media | UGC + social graph, no cart |

## When to add a new domain

Three signals indicate the existing contracts can't accommodate a site:

1. **Forced FAILs.** You find yourself with 5+ FAILs on P0 checks that don't apply (e.g. cart-add FAILs on a site with no cart). The contract is wrong, not your adapter.
50→2. **Cross-cutting access model.** The site's auth model has dimensions not in the existing contracts (e.g. pharma-data's `soft_vip` didn't fit ecommerce's tier system).

| Yes | — | Yes | **Both — pick by primary use case.** |

When multiple domains match, **pick by the user's primary use case for this adapter**, not by what the site as a whole does. A platform with both a shop and a social feed can have both ecommerce and social-media adapters; each follows its own contract.

## Worked examples

| Site | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jd.com` | ✅ | — | — | ecommerce | B2C marketplace, classic cart+order |
| `mall.yaoex.com` | ✅ | — | — | ecommerce | B2B wholesale, cart+order (Phase 3) |
| `db.yaozh.com` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | pharma-data | Data lookup; no cart/order; no UGC |
| `xiaohongshu.com` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | social-media | UGC with social graph; no cart |
| `taobao.com` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ecommerce | Has cart and order (note: shop recommendations are not UGC) |
| `weibo.com` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | social-media | UGC + social graph, no cart |

## When to add a new domain

Three signals indicate the existing contracts can't accommodate a site:

1. **Forced FAILs.** You find yourself with 5+ FAILs on P0 checks that don't apply (e.g. cart-add FAILs on a site with no cart). The contract is wrong, not your adapter.
2. **Cross-cutting access model.** The site's auth model has dimensions not in the existing contracts (e.g. pharma-data's `soft_vip` didn't fit ecommerce's tier system).

1. **The original product thesis is still the right one.** ysbang’s `search-by-price` still FAILs `forbidden-name` today. The contract is doing the job it was created for: cap surface area. Without it, freeze (ma-browser v0.13 F*) would industrialize the 38-file mess.

1. **The official starting point fails the official checker.** All three TEMPLATE.js still call `bb.goto` / `bb.$$eval` / `bb.fetch`. `no-ghost-api` FAIL. SKILL and playbooks still talk like a Playwright handle exists. SM-2.10 migrated *adapters*; the repo that teaches adapters did not catch up. A freeze generator that copies TEMPLATE will emit drafts that cannot `site_run`.
2. **`./tools/bb-eval` is a lie.** File is `-rw-r--r--`. README / wiki / getting-started all say `./tools/bb-eval`. First-time agent hits Permission denied.
3. **Envelope split.** Ecommerce contract + 1688 source use `success`. Social-media contract + wiki envelope page use `ok`. Pharma TEMPLATE uses `success`. An agent (or a freeze generator) that “learns the envelope once” will emit the wrong boolean key half the time. `bb-eval` does not check which key you used.
4. **PHR-8 fights the pharma contract.** Contract: one file per dbKey, name = `yaopinjiage`. Check: canonical set is `auth|list|item|search|export|related`. Real adapter therefore always WARNs. Fitness signal is noisy.
5. **Static green is easy to over-claim.** soul.md already walked this back: XHS 11/15 never had a real-browser run; 1688 write adapters are blocked by React `isTrusted` / partitioned cookies — daemon limits, not eval. The repo’s marketing sentence “0 fail = production ready” was corrected in soul.md and should stay corrected.
6. **Command rename drift.** Runtime CLI is `ma-browser`. Every `@meta.example`, SKILL step, and wiki still says `bb-browser site ...`. v0.13 F7 will print `ma-browser` hints; evolver will keep teaching the old binary unless M0 lands.
7. **Verifier docs are one version behind the tool.** `verify-adapter-runtime-shape.js` header says v3, no `bb` global. wiki `runtime-verification.md` still tables mock `bb.goto`. Two sources of truth.

---

## Gaps vs ma-browser v0.13

| v0.13 need | evolver today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Freeze draft must be runnable `/* @meta */` + async function | Check 0 + URL rule exist | TEMPLATE still ghost-API; freeze-draft `source` field undocumented |
| Daemon wants a machine-readable gate | `--json` exists in usage docs | not verified as a stable schema in this session; no fixture of freeze-draft JSON |
| Health `action` on broken | error/hint/action in contracts | no heuristic table mapping FAIL → login vs re-freeze vs edit source |
| TTL cache / dynamic MCP tools | correctly absent | keep absent |
| Tier 3 auto-gen | correctly refused | SKILL should say “freeze marks incomplete; do the five-step capture” |
| SM-3 portable social contract | XHS-only proven | twitter/bilibili not started |

Phase 4 darwinian: still not justified. Nothing in the hands-on run looked like “single-shot <30%”. The failures are *instruction* failures (ghost API in templates) and *runtime-toolchain* failures (isTrusted), neither of which a mutator population will fix.

---

## What the PRD therefore does

P0: fix the teaching surface (TEMPLATE/SKILL/wiki), make `bb-eval` the freeze quality gate (`--json`, freeze-draft meta, no secrets), patch PHR-8 and `NAVIGATE_REQUIRED` into ecommerce, write the `success`/`ok` cheat sheet without rewriting 80 adapters.

P1: health-heuristic doc for daemon H3; one non-XHS social adapter (SM-3).

Not in scope: cache, MCP dynamic tools, darwinian, 1688 `cart-add` CDP, moving adapters into this repo.

## 2026-09-08 — mtop 签名调用最终结论：partitioned cookie 是不可绕过的浏览器安全边界

### 实验结果

| 尝试 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| Node.js 侧 MD5 签名 + 页内 fetch POST | `FAIL_SYS_ILLEGAL_ACCESS`（render）/ `FAIL_SYS_TOKEN_EMPTY`（async） |
1000→| 原因 | cookieStore 能**读** partitioned cookie（unb/_m_h5_tk），但 fetch 的 `credentials:include` **不发送**它们（CHIPS 分区隔离） |
| 结论 | **浏览器安全模型限制**，非 adapter 层可解决 |

本文件是产品需求，不是合约。合约仍以 `docs/claude/contracts/<domain>/v1.md` 为准。

---

## 0. 一句话
20→
> **evolver 不发明浏览器，也不存 adapter。它定义「一个意图一个 adapter」并用 `bb-eval` 在一秒内否决差的草稿；ma-browser v0.13 负责把刚抓到的网络请求冻成私有 JS、把只读结果按 TTL 沉淀、把调用健康落盘。两边对上，第二个 agent 才不必把同一页再点一遍。**

Phase 4 的 `darwinian_evolver` 仍然是条件项，不是本轮交付。TTL 缓存、动态 MCP 工具、`site_freeze` 运行时都不是本仓库的活。

---

## 1. 为什么现在

1. **运行时已经把飞轮缺口写成 v0.13。** ma-browser 0.12.1 解决的是「别人敢把登录态交给这个进程」。v0.13 要把 `network` 冻成 `$BB_BROWSER_HOME/sites/<site>/<cmd>.js` 草稿（F1–F8）、给只读 `site_run` 加本机 TTL（K1–K6）、给失败加落盘健康（H1–H5）。冻结器会写出带 `/* @meta */` 的 `async function`。若 evolver 的质量闸对不准这份草稿，飞轮会把「ysbang 38 个文件」问题复制到每个被冻过的站点。
30→2. **「好 adapter」已经有三个域的定义，但教法仍在教幽灵 API。** 本分支完成了 ecommerce / pharma-data / social-media 三份 v1 合约、SOC-1..13、运行时语义的 Check 0（剥 `@meta` 后按 `(body)(args)` 编译）、`no-ghost-api`。亲手复跑：`1688/search` **16 pass / 0 warn / 0 fail**。同一套检查对三个官方 TEMPLATE 全部 **FAIL `no-ghost-api`**（`bb.goto` / `bb.$$eval`）。v0.13 冻结器若抄 TEMPLATE，草稿一落地就被自己的闸门打死。
3. **CLI 已经改名，文档还在教 `bb-browser`。** soul.md 2026-09-07 记录：本机 CLI 是 `ma-browser`。SKILL、合约 `@meta.example`、wiki author-loop 仍写 `bb-browser site ...`。冻结成功后的中文提示（v0.13 F7）会和 evolver 教的命令对不上。
4. **静态绿 ≠ 能跑，但静态红一定不该进冻结成功路径。** 1688 的 `cart-add` 在 soul.md 里卡在 React 18 `isTrusted` 和 partitioned cookie——那是 daemon/CDP 上限，不是合约能修的。evolver 该做的是：冻结草稿至少过 `bb-eval`；健康启发式能告诉 daemon「这是登录问题还是结构问题」。不要假装静态检查能替代截图对照。
5. **Phase 4 的触发条件仍未出现。** 决策 `docs/claude/decisions/2026-04-22-why-not-evolver-first.md`：单次 SKILL 成功率 <30% 才接达尔文演化。soul.md 记录的是反面：yaoex 9/9 P0、yaozh 6+1、XHS 15 个 adapter 静态 0 fail。本轮再接 population search 是浪费。

details.context_before:
1. **运行时已经把飞轮缺口写成 v0.13。** ma-browser 0.12.1 解决的是「别人敢把登录态交给这个进程」。v0.13 要把 `network` 冻成 `$BB_BROWSER_HOME/sites/<site>/<cmd>.js` 草稿（F1–F8）、给只读 `site_run` 加本机 TTL（K1–K6）、给失败加落盘健康（H1–H5）。冻结器会写出带 `/* @meta */` 的 `async function`。若 evolver 的质量闸对不准这份草稿，飞轮会把「ysbang 38 个文件」问题复制到每个被冻过的站点。
2. **「好 adapter」已经有三个域的定义，但教法仍在教幽灵 API。** 本分支完成了 ecommerce / pharma-data / social-media 三份 v1 合约、SOC-1..13、运行时语义的 Check 0（剥 `@meta` 后按 `(body)(args)` 编译）、`no-ghost-api`。亲手复跑：`1688/search` **16 pass / 0 warn / 0 fail**。同一套检查对三个官方 TEMPLATE 全部 **FAIL `no-ghost-api`**（`bb.goto` / `bb.$$eval`）。v0.13 冻结器若抄 TEMPLATE，草稿一落地就被自己的闸门打死。
3. **CLI 已经改名，文档还在教 `bb-browser`。** soul.md 2026-09-07 记录：本机 CLI 是 `ma-browser`。SKILL、合约 `@meta.example`、wiki author-loop 仍写 `bb-browser site ...`。冻结成功后的中文提示（v0.13 F7）会和 evolver 教的命令对不上。
details.context_after:
5. **Phase 4 的触发条件仍未出现。** 决策 `docs/claude/decisions/2026-04-22-why-not-evolver-first.md`：单次 SKILL 成功率 <30% 才接达尔文演化。soul.md 记录的是反面：yaoex 9/9 P0、yaozh 6+1、XHS 15 个 adapter 静态 0 fail。本轮再接 population search 是浪费。

3. **Envelope split.** Ecommerce contract + 1688 source use `success`. Social-media contract + wiki envelope page use `ok`. Pharma TEMPLATE uses `success`.
